data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds write to caller-supplied output buffer)
data.rationale: The fuzz target (tests/spng_read_fuzzer.cc) allocates an output buffer of exactly spng_decoded_image_size() bytes (w*h*4 for SPNG_FMT_RGBA8, cap 80MB) and calls spng_decode_image. All chunk-parsing paths I audited (PLTE 655-679, tRNS 817-856, bKGD 783-816, sBIT 728-768 plus check_sbit 2190-2235) are correctly bounds-checked, and the scanline/prev_scanline buffers are allocated with the widest interlace-pass scanline width (calculate_subimages 2069+), so they are not the overflow. The remaining unverified region is the per-pixel processing loop in spng_decode_image (lines 1578-1830) that writes decoded pixels into the caller's 'out' buffer using pixel_offset (line 1450). For interlaced images the loop runs over sub[pass].width/height for each of the 7 passes; if pixel_offset is advanced per scanline using the full image width (or is not reset/advanced consistently with each pass's sub-width), the cumulative writes exceed w*h pixels, overflowing out. ASan would report a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE inside spng_decode_image, reachable from LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput. Confidence is moderate-low: 1M fuzzing executions did not crash, and I could not fully audit the write region within the time limit.
